exposure: Maternal folic acid supplementation during pregnancy (trimesters 1, 2, and 3)
Perinatal factors (e.g., gestational age < 37 weeks, appropriate for gestational age (AGA))
Environmental factors (e.g., maternal smoking status, socioeconomic level of schools, neighborhood traffic and parks)
cohort: The study included 2332 pre-adolescents (mean age 11 years, 50% boys, 451 with asthma) attending elementary schools in Greece.
finding: Maternal folic acid supplementation, particularly in later trimesters, was modestly associated with increased odds of pre-adolescent asthma, with this association being modified by various perinatal and environmental factors.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from pre-adolescents at a mean age of 11 years.
gest_age: Gestational age (< 37 weeks and appropriate for gestational age (AGA)) was considered as a modifying factor.
